head: 48accbbea0fd90fc022abd049a92b2d6c16eeb52
scope: Independent static read-only review, no tests/PG/product edits/push. No repeat deadlock acceptance.
recommendation: Prefer only local duplicate snapshot fingerprint elimination. Do not implement broad load_family result reuse across state without additional proof of equivalent mutable-state and rejection behavior.

facts: The same local snapshot object is fingerprinted first as expected PROTOCOL_ACCEPTED seal value, then immediately in job fingerprint comparison.
Between the calls there is no SQL, external callback, await, write or snapshot mutation.
fingerprint defined at db.py:467 is deterministic JSON serialization (sort keys, UTF-8, disallow NaN) plus SHA256 and has no writes.
verified_pending.safe_scope: Reuse only inside this invocation, never across verified_pending calls, requests, transactions or mutated snapshots.
preserve_order: When accepted_seals length differs from1 original short-circuits before fingerprint. Preserve that early refusal and same Accepted protocol seal changed error.
On one seal, job[kind] is evaluated before fingerprint because it is first value in dict construction. Preserve that order, including KeyError vs serialization exception.
Wrong seal must still fail before protocol snapshot comparison, namespace checks, bounded validation, _authority, result checks and dependency checks.

Suggested two-line approach: bind local snapshot_fp at original fingerprint(snapshot) dictionary value using assignment expression; second comparison uses snapshot_fp. The variable cannot be unset on a continuing path, since a skipped first evaluation unconditionally raises.

Alternative explicit form: reject seal count first; construct expected_seal with phase before fingerprint as original; compare actual seal; compare expected_seal[fingerprint] to job fingerprint. Do not eagerly hash before seal count check.
verified_pending.provable_gain: One JSON serialization+SHA256 removed per invocation that passes the accepted seal check; SQL/authorization counts unchanged. No measured elapsed saving yet.
verified_pending.remaining_verification: Measure direct fingerprint count/time with same input old/new and relevant protocol corruption/rejection cases; preserve original assertions. Existing hotspots observer has not instrumented protocol_jobs.verified_pending or its module-local fingerprint alias.

facts: First load authorizes source/identity before protected saved ledger reads, as explicit comment requires. Removing first changes rejection/read order.
Second load recomputes current app origin, content hashes, grants and authorization fingerprint after state validates state/anchor/accepted receipt/source-version ledger.
state does not write but performs many SQL reads and fingerprint/schema checks, so elapsed time and database snapshots can differ before build.
Store.tx has ordinary c.begin() for PostgreSQL and no explicit stable snapshot isolation setting.
Store.authorize rechecks grant expires_at against time.time at db.py:625; even held grant rows do not freeze wall-clock expiry.
load_family resource selection at lines114-119 has no FOR UPDATE; project lock only coordinates participating app paths, not all direct role/admin data changes or same-transaction mutations.
delivery_graph_current.unsafe_shortcut: Passing first loaded family tuple through state and skipping second load would remove later expiry/source/identity/fresh-origin revalidation, although stale tuple could reconstruct an otherwise valid saved graph.
delivery_graph_current.safe_reuse_boundary: Pure immutable work within a contiguous validation step is preferable. Any retained family result would need explicit trusted private ownership and freshness checks equivalent to the later load for all mutable authority/origin/content inputs, and must not leak between requests/apps/users/projects/transactions. This proof is absent from present code.
delivery_graph_current.potential_gain: Statically avoids one expensive family load per current call, but nested profiling totals cannot serve as causal saving; safety and elapsed gain not established.
delivery_graph_current.tests_evidence: tests/test_report_validated_origin.py:76-112 deliberately inject source/extraction/seal/grant/target mutation after origin validation in the same transaction; existing freshness tests constrain broader caching/reuse. They are not an executed test of this specific current/state boundary.

limits: No general speed claim, globaldeadlock claim, fullsuite or Windows/native conclusion.
Existing900/240/150 budgets and original assertions must remain.
